title: Train a tiny model
summary: Training adjusts weights to reduce a loss, which measures mistakes. This toy example fits numbers near a simple doubling rule.
introduction: Training adjusts weights to reduce a loss, which measures mistakes. This toy example fits numbers near a simple doubling rule. We will use a small example so you can follow each step.
learningObjectives: Use the example to answer a practice question

blocks.text: Training adjusts weights to reduce a loss, which measures mistakes. This toy example fits numbers near a simple doubling rule.

blocks.code:
import tensorflow as tf

import numpy as np
x = np.array([[1.], [2.], [3.], [4.]], dtype="float32")
y = np.array([[2.], [4.], [6.], [8.]], dtype="float32")
model = tf.keras.Sequential([tf.keras.Input(shape=(1,)), tf.keras.layers.Dense(1)])
model.compile(optimizer="sgd", loss="mse")
model.fit(x, y, epochs=20, verbose=0)
print(tuple(model(x).shape))
blocks.title: Train a tiny model

blocks.text: The shape is (4, 1). mse means mean squared error. Twenty training passes do not guarantee exact doubling or real-world accuracy.
